name: Centro Historico
tagline: The UNESCO colonial heart around the Plaza 10 de Noviembre
description: Potosi's atmospheric core, wrapped around the Plaza 10 de Noviembre and the Casa Nacional de la Moneda. Grand colonial churches, ornate facades, cafes, and the best of the city's guesthouses sit within a walkable, cobbled grid, all steep and breathless at this altitude but rich with history at every turn.
bestFor: History lovers and first-time visitors who want to be in the thick of it
pros: Steps from the main sights and the mint
Best concentration of cafes, wifi, and lodging
cons: Steep cobbled streets are punishing at altitude
Can be cold and quiet after dark

name: Cerro Rico side
tagline: The mining slopes below the silver mountain
description: The neighborhoods climbing toward the Cerro Rico, where the city's mining life and tour operators concentrate. This is the gritty, hardworking, higher side of town, closest to the cooperative mines and the sobering tours that define Potosi's story. Raw and real rather than comfortable, with commanding views back over the center.
bestFor: Travelers focused on mine tours and mining history
pros: Closest to the Cerro Rico and mine-tour operators
cons: Even higher and harder on the lungs

name: Villa Imperial / residential outskirts
tagline: Quieter local living beyond the tourist core
description: The calmer residential districts spreading out from the historic center, where everyday Potosinos live. Cheaper rooms and long-stay rentals, neighborhood markets, and simple comedores make this a practical, low-cost base for slow travelers happy to trade sightseeing convenience for local rhythm and a bit more quiet.
bestFor: Budget slow travelers wanting a local, low-key base

name: Sucre (lower-altitude base)
tagline: A gentler, warmer capital about 3 hours away
description: Not part of Potosi but its natural companion base, Sucre sits roughly three hours away at a much lower, kinder altitude. Bolivia's whitewashed constitutional capital is warmer, more comfortable, and far better set up for actually working, making it the sensible place to stay longer and daytrip or side-trip up to Potosi.
bestFor: Remote workers who want a real base near Potosi
pros: Much lower altitude and milder climate
Better wifi, cafes, and nomad amenities
cons: Three hours from Potosi by bus
Not Potosi itself, so requires a trip up
